title: This Eagle's Talons Are Longer Than a Grizzly Bear's Claws

scenes.text: This eagle's talons are longer than a grizzly bear's claws.
Five inches. The harpy eagle's back claw is the size of a steak knife.
Its legs are as thick as a child's wrist. The grip squeezes with hundreds of pounds.
It snatches sloths and monkeys straight off the branch. Prey up to 17 pounds, gone in one grab.
The female weighs up to 20 pounds and can lift prey as heavy as herself.
It hunts the canopy at 50 miles an hour. The monkeys never hear it coming.

description:
The harpy eagle's back talons reach about 13 centimetres, or 5 inches, longer than the claws of many grizzly bears.
With legs as thick as a child's wrist and a grip of several hundred pounds, it plucks sloths and monkeys weighing up to 17 pounds straight out of the rainforest canopy, and females have been recorded lifting prey as heavy as themselves.
Which bird would you least want to meet in the wild?
first_comment: Harpy eagles have a wingspan of up to six and a half feet but keep their wings short for their size so they can weave between trees. Bear claws or eagle talons: which would you rather face?
